answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable stake before it may act, like a crystal that only forms under pressure: cheap to create once, expensive to mass-produce. A public beacon publishes each agent stake and past attestations, so a flood of fresh identities looks like a comet shower, bright, brief, and unproven, while established agents accumulate verifiable history. Attackers must then pay per identity and risk slashing, so forging a thousand credible agents costs a thousand stakes, not one script.
